name: OmniStream MQ
target_user: Systems Engineers and Distributed Infrastructure Architects
problem: Traditional enterprise message queues require heavy external cluster management, while raw socket protocols lack consumer group balancing, acknowledgment persistence, and durability guarantees.
pain: Developers building local-first event-driven pipelines lack lightweight brokers that support multiplexed consumer subscriptions, dead-letter queues, and deterministic message replay without heavy external runtimes.
solution: A high-performance Java 21 broker implementing a binary wire protocol, zero-copy segment file I/O, consumer group rebalancing, and configurable retention policies entirely from scratch.
verification: Deterministic integration suite testing concurrent producers, consumer group partition handoffs, abrupt client disconnection recovery, and corrupted offset index repair using automated byte-injection scripts.
major_features: Custom binary wire protocol supporting framed message frames and multiplexed connection streams
Segmented append-only on-disk log storage with configurable byte-size and time-based rotation
Consumer group coordination engine implementing dynamic partition assignment and heartbeat liveness tracking
Explicit message acknowledgment (ACK) and negative acknowledgment (NACK) offset tracking loops
Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) diversion mechanism for messages exceeding maximum delivery retry thresholds
Configurable message retention policy enforcing background disk compaction and segment pruning
Non-blocking TCP network server utilizing Java 21 Selector and SocketChannel multiplexing
Deterministic integration harness injecting network packet drops, socket delays, and disk full simulations
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
